title: Contraction Champion
goal: I can make, fix and use contractions, even won't and let's.

card.desc: Bristol proves she can use every contraction from this week, all mixed up, plus the odd ones won't (will not) and let's (let us). She picks the contraction that makes sense in a sentence, fixes mistakes like cant and wo'nt, and writes her own sentences with contractions in the packet.

slides.title: Contraction Champion: On Your Own
slides.text: You proved it in class. Now be a contraction champion on your own! 🏆

slides.title: Contractions
slides.text: The apostrophe takes the place of the missing letters.

steps.text: Look after the apostrophe: n't → not, 'm → am, 're → are, 's → is, 'll → will, 've → have.
won't = will not. It breaks the rule.
let's = let us. The u drops out.

slides.tip: Not sure? Say the sentence the long way.

slides.title: Say it out loud
slides.text: Say these out loud. You can tell your mom!
prompts: Ask your mom to do something with you. Start with Let's.

slides.title: Make the contraction
slides.text: Type the contraction. Put the apostrophe in the right spot.

items.q: The cat ____ eat its food. (will not)
items.why: will not → won't. won't breaks the rule: will changes to wo, then add n't.
items.no: This is the rule-breaker. will changes to wo. Then add n't.

items.why: Let us → Let's. The apostrophe takes the place of the u.
items.no: Push Let us together. Take out the u. Put in an apostrophe.

items.why: They are → They're. The apostrophe takes the place of the a.
items.no: Push They are together. Take out the a. Put in an apostrophe.
It ends with n't. What word does n't stand for?
This time the s does not stand for is. Let ___ eat! Who will eat?
items.hint: You and me will eat. That is us.

items.no: Only an m is after the apostrophe.

slides.title: Right spot or wrong spot?
slides.text: Tap a word. Then tap the right box.

items.why: Wrong spot. It should be let's.
items.hint: Does the apostrophe go at the end?

items.why: Right spot. It takes the place of h and a.
items.hint: Where were the h and a in I have?

items.why: Right spot, between n and t.
items.hint: won't ends with n't. Is the apostrophe between n and t?

items.why: Wrong spot. It should be I've.
items.hint: The h and a were right after I.

items.why: Right spot. It takes the place of the u.
items.hint: Where was the u in let us?

items.why: Wrong spot. It should be won't.
items.hint: won't ends with n't. Look at where the apostrophe is.

slides.title: Pick the one that makes sense

items.q: The kids ____ ready. They still need their shoes.
no: Say it the long way: The kids is not ready. We say the kids are.
Say it the long way: The kids will not ready. That does not make sense.
Say it the long way: It is make a snack. That does not make sense.
Say it the long way: Will not make a snack. That does not make sense.

items.q: Amy wrote: Were going home. She meant We are. What is right?
no: were is a different word. We are → We're.
Only the a drops out. The apostrophe goes right after We.

items.q: Liz wrote: He doesnt like peas. What is right?
no: The apostrophe does not go at the end.
The o was between n and t. The apostrophe goes there.

items.q: Scarves cost $8 each. Amy buys 6. What is the total?
items.why: Same price for each scarf. 6 × 8. 5 × 8 = 40. One more 8: 48.
items.no: Every scarf is $8. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.no: This is the rule-breaker. will changes to wo. Then add n't.

sets.q: What two words make won't? Type them.
sets.no: won't is the rule-breaker. It is not want.

sets.q: I ____ eat the cake. I am full.
no: want means you wish for something. I want eat does not make sense.
Say it the long way: I was not eat. That does not make sense.

sets.q: Liz wrote: Ill help you. What is right?
no: Two l's stay together after the apostrophe.
Ill with no apostrophe means sick. I will → I'll.
lets with no apostrophe means allows, like Mom lets me play.
let stays whole. The apostrophe goes after let.

sets.q: ____ been to the zoo two times. (I have)
sets.why: I have → I've. The apostrophe takes the place of the h and a.
sets.no: Push I have together. Take out the h and a. Put in an apostrophe.

sets.q: What two words make let's? Type them.
sets.no: Only an s is after the apostrophe. It stands for us here.

sets.q: My shoes ____ clean. They are muddy.
no: We say my shoes are, not my shoes is.
Say it the long way: My shoes will not clean. That does not make sense.

sets.q: Amy wrote: We wo'nt be late. What is right?
sets.why: will not → won't. The apostrophe goes between n and t.
no: The apostrophe does not go at the end.
The apostrophe goes between n and t.
want means you wish for something.
wasn't means was not.

sets.no: Push Let us together. Take out the u. Put in an apostrophe.

sets.q: ____ a big fan of soccer. (She is)
sets.why: She is → She's. The apostrophe takes the place of the i.
sets.no: Push She is together. Take out the i. Put in an apostrophe.

sets.q: What two words make we're? Type them.
It ____ my birthday today. My birthday is next week.
no: We say it is, not it are.
Say it the long way: It will not my birthday. That does not make sense.

sets.q: Ellie wrote: Lets go! She meant let us go. What is right?
no: The apostrophe goes where the u was, right after let.
lets with no apostrophe means allows. She needs Let's.
I'll means I will.
I've means I have.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one. Only your first try counts. Not sure? Say it the long way.

questions.q: Liz wrote: I cant swim yet. What is right?
no: The apostrophe goes where the n and o were, after can.
can stays whole. The apostrophe goes after can.

no: were is a different word. We are → We're.
Only the a drops out. The e stays.

teacher.objective: Bristol proves she can make and take apart every contraction from this week, mixed: the not family, the am/are/is/will/have families, and the odd ones won't (will not) and let's (let us). She chooses the contraction that makes sense in a sentence, fixes contraction mistakes, and writes her own sentences with contractions. Week 6 Day 3 (Prove it).
materials: The Class lesson open on your laptop (course page, code 9110)
8 index cards: will not, let us, they are, I have, does not, she is, we will, can not
Tuesday's word cards and sticky notes
Printed packet (2 pages) to send home

plan.do: Class slide 1. Which letters drop out of will and have?
Class slide 2. A contraction from her book that is not an n't word; why authors use contractions when characters talk.
Class slide 3. Check Tuesday's After-Class score and Wednesday's packets first.
Class slides 4–5. won't is the rule-breaker (not want); let's = let us.
Class slide 6. Whiteboard first, then she types.
Class slides 7–8. Look after the apostrophe to find the hiding word.
Class slide 9. She picks a card, writes the contraction and says a sentence.
Class slides 10–11. She reads each sentence the long way.
Class slides 12–13. She says what is wrong before she picks.
Class slide 14. Four contractions on the whiteboard, then typed.
Class slide 15. Three sentences on the whiteboard: won't, let's, they're.
Class slide 17. Show the weekend task list.

watch: won't mixed up with want, or written as wont or wo'nt. won't = will not; it ends with n't.
lets for let's. Say the long way: "let us go" → Let's go.
Picking a contraction that does not fit ("The kids isn't ready"). Have her say the sentence the long way.
were for we're and your for you're.
Apostrophes missing in her own sentences (cant, Ill). In the packet, check every contraction she writes.
Typed answers ignore apostrophes. The apostrophe spot is checked by the multiple-choice items, the sort and the packet.

packet_key.answer: Any sentence that uses won't (will not) correctly, with a capital letter and a period.
Any sentence that uses let's (let us) correctly, for example: Let's play a game.
Any sentence that uses they're (they are) correctly. Not their or there.
Any sentence that uses I'll (I will) correctly, with a capital I.
Any contraction from her book with the right two words.

teacher.notes: Weekend work is medium: the After-Class Lesson tonight, the Practice and page 2 of the Lesson 14 Packet on Friday, this Packet on Saturday, and the reading lesson on Sunday. Next week (Lessons 16–18) is spelling teams ea and oo. Keep checking contractions in every piece of her writing from now on.

slides.title: Contraction Champion
slides.text:
Today you prove it! 🏆
Every contraction, all mixed up.

notes.do: Before she arrives, write these on 8 index cards (one per card): will not, let us, they are, I have, does not, she is, we will, can not. Keep Tuesday's word cards and sticky notes. Whiteboard ready.
notes.say: "Monday: the not family. Tuesday: the families for I, you, he, she, it, we and they. Today: everything mixed, two rule-breakers, and you write your own."
notes.ask: "Which letters drop out of will? Of have?"
notes.listen: w and i; h and a.

slides.title: Contractions in my book
slides.text: Think about the book you are reading.
prompts: What happened in your book this week?
Find a contraction that is not an n't word. What two words make it?
Read what a character says. Now say it with no contractions. Does it sound different?

notes.do: About 6 minutes. She finds a contraction like I'm, it's, you're or I'll in a part where someone talks.
notes.ask: "What two words make it?" "Why do you think the author used a contraction there?"
notes.listen: The two words are right. People talk with contractions, so the talking sounds real.

no: they're means they are.
they'll means they will.

items.no: ll is after the apostrophe. Which word ends with ll?

notes.do: Check Tuesday's After-Class score and Wednesday's packet work first.
notes.listen: they've; will. Look at Wednesday's packet for apostrophes in the wrong spot.

slides.title: The rule-breaker: won't

steps.text: Then add n't, like the not family: won't.

slides.tip: won't means will not. It does not mean want!

notes.do: She writes will not on the whiteboard, then writes won't under it.
notes.say: "won't is a rule-breaker. You just have to know it."
notes.ask: "What does won't mean? Is it the same as want?"
notes.listen: "will not." won't and want sound close. Say both slowly: I won't go. I want to go.

slides.title: Let's go!

steps.text: The u drops out. The apostrophe takes its place.
We say let's when we ask friends to do something with us: Let's play!

slides.tip: lets with no apostrophe is a different word: Mom lets me play.

notes.do: She builds let's with a card that says let us and a sticky note over the u.
notes.ask: "Which letter did you cover?" "Say a sentence that starts with Let's."
notes.listen: The u. Any let's sentence that asks someone to do something together.

items.q: The baby ____ go to sleep. (will not)
items.why: will not → won't. won't breaks the rule: will changes to wo, then add n't.
items.no: This is the rule-breaker. will changes to wo. Then add n't.

items.why: Let us → Let's. The apostrophe takes the place of the u.
items.no: Push Let us together. Take out the u. Put in an apostrophe.

no: want sounds close, but it means you wish for something.
was not makes wasn't.

notes.do: She writes each one on the whiteboard, then types it.

slides.title: All the families
slides.text: Look after the apostrophe to find the hiding word.

steps.text: n't → not: don't, isn't, aren't, wasn't, didn't, doesn't, can't, won't
'm → am: I'm · 're → are: you're, we're, they're · 's → is: he's, she's, it's
'll → will: I'll, you'll, we'll · 've → have: I've, we've, they've

slides.tip: The odd ones: can't (n and o drop out), won't (will changes) and let's (us).

notes.do: She reads each row out loud. Then you cover the slide and she names one word from each family.
notes.listen: One word from each family, from memory.

slides.title: Which word is hiding?
slides.text: Tap a word. Then tap the box with the word that made it.

items.hint: Only an m is after the apostrophe.

items.why: won't = will not. It ends with n't.

items.hint: Only an s is after the apostrophe.

notes.do: She taps and says the two long words for each one.
notes.listen: won't = will not is the tricky one: it goes in the not box.

slides.title: Contraction cards
slides.text: Pick a card. Write the contraction on the whiteboard.
prompts: Pick a card. Read the two words.
Write the contraction. Where does the apostrophe go?

notes.do: About 6 minutes. Shuffle the 8 cards from slide 1 (will not, let us, they are, I have, does not, she is, we will, can not). She picks one at a time, writes the contraction on the whiteboard and says a sentence with it.
notes.listen: won't, let's, they're, I've, doesn't, she's, we'll, can't, each with the apostrophe in the right spot. If she writes wo'nt or wont, show her the n't ending again.

slides.title: Which one makes sense?
slides.text: Read the sentence the long way. Does it make sense?

steps.text:
The dog ____ stop barking.
won't → The dog will not stop barking. ✅
want → The dog want stop barking. ❌

Liz ____ at home. She is at school.
isn't → Liz is not at home. ✅
aren't → Liz are not at home. ❌

slides.tip: Say it the long way. Your ears will tell you!

notes.do: She reads each sentence out loud both ways.
notes.listen: "Liz is one girl, so is." Let her ears do the work.

slides.title: Pick the one that makes sense

items.q: Amy ____ go out. She has a cold.
no: Say it the long way: Amy is not go out. That does not make sense.
we'll means we will. The sentence is about Amy.

items.q: Look at the clouds! ____ going to rain.
no: Say it the long way: I am going to rain. That does not make sense.
Say it the long way: They have going to rain. That does not make sense.

items.q: Dad says, "____ have pancakes for dinner!"
no: lets with no apostrophe means allows. We need let us → let's.
Let is one word. We need the contraction for let us.

notes.do: She reads each sentence out loud with her choice, then the long way.

slides.title: Find the mistake

steps.text:
We'r late. ❌ → We're ✅
Only the a drops out. The e stays.

He wo'nt eat. ❌ → won't ✅
The apostrophe goes between n and t.

slides.tip: Check: is the apostrophe there? Is it in the right spot? Are the right letters gone?

notes.do: She writes each fixed sentence on the whiteboard.
notes.listen: Missing apostrophe; a missing letter that should stay; the apostrophe in the wrong spot.

items.q: Marion wrote: Shes my friend. What is right?
items.why: She is → She's. The apostrophe takes the place of the i.
no: The apostrophe does not go at the end.
The apostrophe is missing. She is → She's.

items.q: Ellie wrote: Theyv'e left. What is right?
items.why: They have → They've. The h and a drop out right after they.
no: The h and a were right after they. The apostrophe goes there.
A contraction needs an apostrophe.

items.q: Liz wrote: I want go. She meant I will not go. What is right?
no: want means you wish for something. She meant will not → won't.
The apostrophe goes between n and t: won't.

notes.do: She says what is wrong BEFORE she picks.
notes.listen: Missing apostrophe; wrong spot; want for won't.

items.no: The rule-breaker: will changes to wo. Then add n't.
Take out the u. Put in an apostrophe.
Take out the a in are. Put in an apostrophe.
Take out the i in is. Put in an apostrophe.

notes.do: Fast. She writes all four on the whiteboard first, then types them.
notes.listen: won't, let's, you're, it's. Check the whiteboard for each apostrophe.

slides.title: Write your own
slides.text: Write each sentence on the whiteboard.

notes.do: About 5 minutes. She writes; you check the capital letter, the apostrophe and the period. She will do this again in the packet.
notes.listen: Each contraction is spelled right and makes sense. They're must mean they are.

items.no: won't is the rule-breaker. It is not want.

items.why: let us → Let's. The apostrophe takes the place of the u.
no: The apostrophe goes where the u was, not at the end.
let stays whole. The apostrophe goes after let.

notes.listen: will not; Let's play! If she misses either, go back to slide 4 or 5.
